# hyperlite_vm (Resource)

A virtual machine: made from Hyperlite's cloud image, an installation ISO, a template or another VM; customised before its first boot; started once made.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "hyperlite_template" "debian" {
  name = "debian-12-base"
}

# A VM deployed from a template, customised at its first boot, as vSphere's clone { customize }.
resource "hyperlite_vm" "web" {
  name      = "web-1"
  vcpu      = 2
  memory_mb = 4096
  tags      = ["web", "prod"]

  clone {
    template = data.hyperlite_template.debian.name
  }

  customize {
    hostname = "web-1"
    domain   = "example.internal"
    dns      = ["10.0.20.53"]

    network {
      addresses = ["10.0.20.11/24"]
      gateway   = "10.0.20.1"
    }
  }

  # The first disk is the system disk; it only grows.
  disk { size_gb = data.hyperlite_template.debian.disks[0].size_gb + 10 }
  disk { size_gb = 50 }

  network_interface { network = "lan" }
}

# A VM made from Hyperlite's cloud image, with its account.
resource "hyperlite_vm" "worker" {
  name      = "worker-1"
  vcpu      = 1
  memory_mb = 2048

  cloud_init {
    user     = "ops"
    password = var.vm_password
    ssh_keys = [var.ssh_public_key]
  }

  disk { size_gb = 20 }
  network_interface { network = "lan" }
}

variable "vm_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "ssh_public_key" {
  type = string
}

output "web_address" {
  value = hyperlite_vm.web.ip_address
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory in MB. A change stops the VM, applies, and starts it again.
- `name` (String) The VM's name. A change renames it (the VM is stopped for it, then started again).
- `vcpu` (Number) Virtual CPUs. A change stops the VM, applies, and starts it again.

### Optional

- `autostart` (Boolean) Started when its node starts.
- `clone` (Block, Optional) Make the VM from a template or from another (stopped) VM, with a copy of its disks. Its system, account and firmware come from the source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--clone))
- `cloud_init` (Block, Optional) The account of a VM made from a cloud image (Hyperlite's or a template's): applied before its first boot, then at its next boot after a change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--cloud_init))
- `customize` (Block, Optional) The guest's customisation, written on its cloud-init drive as vSphere's `customize` and Proxmox VE's cloud-init options are: before its first boot, then at its next boot after a change. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--customize))
- `disk` (Block List) The VM's disks, in order: the first is its system disk. A disk grows in place (never shrinks); one added is created and attached; one removed is detached and deleted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--disk))
- `firmware` (String) `bios`, `uefi` or `uefi_secure` (Secure Boot and TPM 2.0, what Windows 11 asks). A VM made from Hyperlite's cloud image or an ISO only; a clone keeps its source's.
- `force_stop` (Boolean) Stop the VM hard when its clean shutdown did not end within `shutdown_timeout`.
- `guest_os` (String) The system an ISO installs, for the devices it gets (`auto` reads it from the ISO's name).
- `iso` (String) An installation ISO of the node's library: the VM gets a blank system disk and is installed from its console. Without `iso` nor `clone`, the VM is made from Hyperlite's cloud image (Debian 12) and needs `cloud_init`.
- `network_interface` (Block List) The VM's interfaces, in order: at least one. A change of network keeps the interface's MAC address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--network_interface))
- `node` (String) The member of the cluster the VM runs on: it is made there, and every change is done there (Hyperlite sends the request on). Absent: the node the provider talks to, and the node it is read on afterwards (HA may move it). A change **migrates** the VM, live, as vSphere moves a VM when its host changes: Hyperlite migrates running VMs only.
- `notes` (String) Notes, as the dashboard shows them.
- `resource_pool` (Number) The pool (its id) the VM is a member of: its assignments give rights on the VM. Required from an account that is not an administrator (vm.allocate on the pool).
- `shutdown_timeout` (String) How long a clean shutdown may take before a change that needs the VM stopped, or its deletion.
- `storage_pool` (String) The storage pool of the disks made with the VM (`default` when absent). A disk added later goes on its own `storage_pool`, or this one.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags, as the dashboard shows them (and backup jobs select VMs by).
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `wait_for_ip` (String) How long to wait, once the VM is started, for its address (`0s`: do not wait). Not waited for when `customize` gives the first interface a static address.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The VM's UUID: it stays the same when the VM is renamed.
- `ip_address` (String) The VM's address: the static one of `customize`, else its DHCP lease or its guest agent's.
- `state` (String) `active`, `stopped`, `paused`, `crashed`...

<a id="nestedblock--clone"></a>
### Nested Schema for `clone`

Optional:

- `template` (String) The template's name (data source `hyperlite_template`).
- `vm` (String) The name of a stopped VM to clone.


<a id="nestedblock--cloud_init"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cloud_init`

Optional:

- `password` (String, Sensitive) Its password (never read back: a change made elsewhere is not seen).
- `ssh_keys` (List of String) Its SSH public keys.
- `user` (String) The account's name. Required in the block.


<a id="nestedblock--customize"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customize`

Optional:

- `dns` (List of String) Resolvers.
- `dns_search` (List of String) Search domains.
- `domain` (String) Domain, for the FQDN.
- `hostname` (String) Host name (the VM's name when absent).
- `network` (Block List) A static configuration of one interface; the others use DHCP. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--customize--network))
- `user_data` (String) A cloud-config added to Hyperlite's own (packages, runcmd, write_files...); its account and host-name keys are refused.

<a id="nestedblock--customize--network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `customize.network`

Required:

- `addresses` (List of String) Addresses with their prefix: `10.0.20.11/24`.

Optional:

- `gateway` (String) Default gateway.
- `interface` (Number) The index of the `network_interface` (0, the first, when absent).



<a id="nestedblock--disk"></a>
### Nested Schema for `disk`

Required:

- `size_gb` (Number) Size in GB.

Optional:

- `storage_pool` (String) Its storage pool; a change moves the disk (administrators).

Read-Only:

- `target` (String) Its device name in the VM (`sda`, `vdb`...).


<a id="nestedblock--network_interface"></a>
### Nested Schema for `network_interface`

Required:

- `network` (String) The network's name (data source `hyperlite_network`).

Optional:

- `vlan_tag` (Number) 802.1Q tag, on a network that carries tags.

Read-Only:

- `mac` (String) Its MAC address.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# By the VM's name or UUID; `<node>/<name>` for a VM of another node.
terraform import hyperlite_vm.web web-1
```
